newsitem.title: FRANCE: Germany, France sign helicopter industrial deal.
newsitem.headline: Germany, France sign helicopter industrial deal.

text.p: French and German officials on Friday signed contracts worth 730 million marks ($422 million) to set up production lines to build the Franco-German Tiger combat helicopter.
The bilateral project has been plagued by cuts in French and German defence budgets as both countries struggle to cut public deficits in time to launch the single European currency by 1999.
Eurocopter, a joint venture 70-percent held by French state-owned Aerospatiale and 30 percent by Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), will build the Tiger.
The contracts cover the helicopter airframe, the MTR 390 motor from the MTR engine group and anti-tank missile systems.
MTR is a consortium of engine makers MTU of Germany, Turbomeca of France and Rolls-Royce Plc .

France is ordering an initial 80 ground support Tigers and Germany is buying the same number of multi-role models. The French will eventually get 215 Tigers, in ground support and anti-tank versions. Germany will receive 212 multi-role Tigers.

The initial French order is estimated at 12 billion francs ($2.06 billion), after a 10 percent price cut demanded by the DGA French procurement agency, Eurocopter chairman Francois Bigay has said. The DGA said the cut resulted in a saving of 1.4 billion francs ($241 million).
The order contracts are due in 1998, the DGA said.
First deliveries to the German army are due in 2001 while the aircraft will enter service with French forces in 2002.

Development costs total 2.5 billion marks ($1.45 billion) since 1989, equally shared between the two countries, a Eurocopter spokeswoman said. She added the pre-production contracts signed today were worth 730 million marks and were due to have been signed 18 months ago.
The contracts allow the purchase of assembly jigs and tools to equip the two Eurocopter plants making the Tiger, one each in France and Germany.

Aerospatiale had hoped to do similar joint ventures in missiles and space activities with Dasa, as part of an industrial consolidation, but saw its long-time German partner teaming instead with French rival Lagardere . ($1 = DM 1.73, FFR 5.82)
